findings.title: AdministratorAccess attached to demo role
findings.explanation: The role gained AWS AdministratorAccess. This permits all actions and resources within effective account controls; SCPs, boundaries and explicit denies may still limit access.
findings.remediation: Detach AdministratorAccess from this demo role and restore the approved attachments. Review terraform -chdir=terraform plan, then run terraform -chdir=terraform apply. Rescan after AWS propagation.

findings.title: Security group permits public SSH
findings.explanation: The new rule permits TCP/22 from the entire internet, increasing exposure to password attacks, stolen credentials and exploitable SSH services. Actual reachability also needs an attached workload, routing and a listening service; this demo SG is unattached.
findings.remediation: Remove the public SSH rule or restore the trusted administrator CIDR. Review terraform -chdir=terraform plan, then run terraform -chdir=terraform apply. Rescan after AWS propagation.

findings.title: S3 public access protection was weakened
findings.explanation: One or more bucket-level public access guardrails changed from enabled to disabled. This increases the chance that a later policy or ACL change exposes data. It does not alone prove public reachability; account-level controls may still block access.
findings.remediation: Re-enable the expected Block Public Access settings and review the bucket policy and ACL. Review terraform -chdir=terraform plan, then run terraform -chdir=terraform apply. Rescan after AWS propagation.

findings.title: Potential IAM privilege escalation permissions
findings.explanation: New permissions include policy/trust mutation, or role passing with workload creation, or broad AssumeRole. These can support escalation when combined with a usable target role or other permissions. This heuristic does not prove an exploitable path.
findings.remediation: Remove unnecessary IAM mutation/role delegation permissions; constrain role ARNs, iam:PassedToService and trust conditions where applicable. Review terraform -chdir=terraform plan, then run terraform -chdir=terraform apply. Rescan after AWS propagation.

findings.title: IAM action scope broadened with a wildcard
findings.explanation: An added Allow statement contains a wildcard action. Action:* includes every action within its resource and condition scope; service wildcards can also include future service operations.
findings.remediation: Replace wildcard actions with the minimum explicit actions needed. Review terraform -chdir=terraform plan, then run terraform -chdir=terraform apply. Rescan after AWS propagation.

findings.title: IAM Allow statement uses broad resources
findings.explanation: An added Allow statement uses wildcard resource scope for actions not all recognized as inherently unscopable reads by this tool. Conditions and IAM resource-level support must be reviewed before deciding effective exposure.
findings.remediation: Use specific ARNs where supported and restrictive conditions where resource-level permissions are unavailable. Review terraform -chdir=terraform plan, then run terraform -chdir=terraform apply. Rescan after AWS propagation.
